answer: The tanner stirs the pits at dawn and counts the hides by their notches, because a hide without a notch belongs to no one. Census enumerator appointment with statistics office attestation is the notch: one-year appointment, 500 households visited, training exam, registry entry. The willow is one hide, soaked and scraped by hands that know the bark liquor. A forged notch is spotted when the hide is stretched, and the harbor is the forfeit, two years of pit fees paid to the guild and the yard shut for a season. The nebula is the guild register, entered by the master tanner and open to any buyer.
